claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has an anomalous brittle aging window between approximately 550°C and 750°C.
The brittle window is caused by the synergistic combination of high L12 ordering and jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
The L12-ordered regions in the brittle condition approach Ni3Al stoichiometry.
High L12 ordering elevates the antiphase boundary energy.
Elevated antiphase boundary energy suppresses cross-slip and forces planar slip.
Jagged B2/FCC boundary serrations concentrate stress when planar slip bands impinge on them.
Stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC boundaries initiates cracking and causes low elongation.
Aging above 750°C reduces long-range order and smooths the B2/FCC interfaces.
Reduced ordering and smoother interfaces restore cross-slip and ductility.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a dual-phase B2 plus FCC microstructure and high ductility.
Aging at 600°C induces brittleness, whereas aging at 750°C restores ductility.
The as-cast material has a random atomic distribution and smooth phase boundaries.
A 600°C-aged sample will exhibit high APBE, jagged boundaries, planar slip traces, and low elongation.
A 750°C-aged sample will exhibit reduced order, smoother boundaries, restored cross-slip, and high elongation.
The ductility transition occurs when the L12 ordering parameter falls below approximately 0.6 and boundary serration amplitude falls below a critical value.
Falling below the proposed ordering and boundary-roughness thresholds allows cross-slip to dominate over planar slip.
Local L12 ordering can be quantified by CBED and APBE can be inferred from dislocation dissociation width in HRTEM.
A short 700°C anneal can artificially smooth B2/FCC interfaces while retaining a useful control for the 600°C ordering condition.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis places the return to ductility at temperatures above 750°C, whereas the intervention and predicted outcome state that aging at 750°C itself restores ductility.
The boundary field proposes an L12-ordering threshold of less than 0.6, but the uncertainty field states that the exact critical ordering threshold is not quantified by the evidence.
The initial state is described as containing an ordered B2 phase, while the baseline describes the material broadly as having a random atomic distribution.
